content:
We have many templates returned. Need to find one that when applied to the given molecule (target) reproduces the forward reaction (i.e., retrosynthetic step). The task: return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The search returned entries with fields: reaction_id, template_hash, retro_smarts_template, canonical_smarts_template, mapped_rxn, etc. The template_id likely corresponds to reaction_id? Or maybe template_id is separate. In examples, they used integer template_id. Probably reaction_id is the template ID. We'll need to pick the appropriate template that matches the described carbonyl-ene reaction.

The description: carbonyl-ene reaction: alkene + allylic hydrogen + carbonyl -> new C-C bond, new stereocenter, hydroxyl formed, five-membered ring formed, ketone and C=C double bond gone, aliphatic hydroxyl and five-membered ring formed. So the retrosynthetic step would break a C-O bond (hydroxyl) and a C-C bond (ring) to give a carbonyl and alkene.

We need a template that does that. Look at returned templates. The first entry (reaction_id 1229769) seems to involve a silicon group and carbonyl etc, not relevant.

Second entry (reaction_id 1237522) seems to involve a carbonyl-ene? The mapped_rxn shows a product with a C=C and carbonyl? Let's inspect: mapped_rxn: '[CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]([F:4])([F:5])[C@:6]1([OH:7])...' product side after >> is same as reactant? Actually mapped_rxn shows reactants then product? The format is reactants>>products. In entry 1237522, mapped_rxn: '[CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]...>>[CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]...' It seems same? Might be a reversible? Hard.

Third entry (reaction_id 175088) not.

Fourth entry (reaction_id 12858) retro_smarts_template: '[C:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[C:3]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[C:3]' That's a carbonyl formation from alkane? Not.

Fifth entry (reaction_id 1042412) looks like a carbonyl-ene? Mapped_rxn: '[CH3:31][C@:30]12[CH2:32][C:7](OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F)=[C:8]3...' Not.

Sixth entry (reaction_id 145237) not.

Seventh entry (reaction_id 1336732) not.

Thus maybe the appropriate template is reaction_id 1237522? Let's examine its mapped_rxn more: It shows product with a hydroxyl and ring? The product_smiles: '[CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]([F:4])([F:5])[C@:6]1([OH:7])...[C@H:31]12[CH3:32]' This seems to have a hydroxyl and a five-membered ring? The product includes a fused ring system with many atoms, maybe not.

Our target molecule is given with atom mapping: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... ) [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

So target has an alkene (CH2= C attached to aromatic ring) and a cyclopentanol with CF3 group. The carbonyl-ene would involve intramolecular reaction between the alkene and the carbonyl (maybe a ketone) to form a new C-C bond and a hydroxyl. But our target already has OH; maybe the precursor is a ketone and alkene.

Thus retrosynthetic step: break the C-O bond (OH) to carbonyl, break C-C bond forming ring? The template should convert a hydroxy cyclopentane to a carbonyl and alkene.

Look at entry 1237522: product_smiles includes OH at position 22 (maybe). The reactant_smiles includes a carbonyl? Let's see reactant_smiles: 'C[Si](C)(C)[C:23]([F:24])([F:25])[F:26].[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[c:5]1... [C:21](=[O:22])...' So reactant has a carbonyl (C=O) at position 22. Product has OH at 22. So this is a carbonyl to alcohol conversion, maybe a reduction? Not carbonyl-ene.

Our target has OH at 14, not carbonyl. So we need a template that converts OH to carbonyl and forms a double bond elsewhere.

Check entry 12858: retro_smarts_template: '[C:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[C:3]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[C:3]'. This transforms a CH2 between two carbons into a carbonyl attached to one carbon and the other carbon remains. That seems like a carbonyl-ene? Not exactly.

But maybe the correct template is not in these results; we may need to search differently. Use functional_groups_broken = ["ketones", "C-C double bonds"] and formed = ["aliphatic hydroxyls", "five-membered rings"] gave empty. Maybe need to search with bonds broken/formed using correct format "6-6". But we don't know bond indices.

Alternative: Use search without criteria and then filter manually by checking if template matches our molecule. Could retrieve many templates? But we have limited results.

Maybe we can directly check each returned template's retro_smarts_template to see if it matches our molecule using check_smiles_reaction_template_matching. Use template IDs (reaction_id). Let's test each.
